top.title: The strange reason Japan can’t pick their best fly half against England
top.description: In the aftermath of his side’s defeat to Wales, the Japan head coach Eddie Jones already had more than half an eye on England . “We’ll need to be able to break up the game,” the veteran schemer said with a glint in his eye and a familiar smirk on his face. “If we play an orthodox game of rugby, we’re probably going to struggle to beat them. And the English don’t react well to unorthodox rugby. We’ve got to think about how we can play quite unorthodoxly.” Jones speaks, of course, from experience. It was his England side that were baffled by Italy’s radical ruck tactics in the Six Nations in 2017 ; in a neat twist, Conor O’Shea, the architect of that plan, now heads up performance at England’s Rugby Football Union (RFU). “Maybe we’ll play like Italy did in 2017,” Jones teased. “Can you still play like that in the rucks? I don’t think you can, can you?” Eddie Jones has promised to throw a few curveballs at England (Getty) England are bracing for something similarly avant-garde nonetheless. It is instructive, though, that Jones is having to talk in such terms about a side he does not yet see as an equal to the world’s top teams. Japan beat Italy and pushed Ireland close in July, before coming within three points of Australia in August – they have the talent to at least give England a fright. There is one key difference from those games, though. In each of those encounters, Japan were steered from fly half by Ryunosuke Ito, a 21-year-old playmaker long tipped for a bright future who was named to start against France before he had even played a senior club game. He took to Test rugby like a natural; through the Nations Championship, Australia series and Pacific Nations Cup, the No 10 shirt was his. For a team that had struggled to replace Yu Tamura, and with Lee Seung Sin injured, here was the welcome emergence of a new, young star. Ryunosuke Ito has emerged as a budding star for Japan (Getty) That flourishing has been brought to a strange and unwelcome halt, though. Ito is not in the United Kingdom with the rest of Jones’s squad, with Riku Kitahara steering the ship against Wales in Cardiff instead. Kitahara performed well; about as well as one might expect of a player reportedly described by Jones as his fourth-choice fly half. There is no injury to speak of to Ito. Why, then, is he absent? Well, it has to do with a strange rugby hierarchy that persists in Japan. While his colleagues are battling the best in men’s Test rugby in Europe, Ito will be obliged to pull on the shirt of Meiji University as he completes his education. “He’s the only 10 for a tier one nation in the world who has to go and play for an amateur team now,” Jones complained after the recent defeat to Fiji, according to rugbyjp.com . “Imagine if [baseball superstar] Shohei Ohtani went back to play for Keio University.” It is a challenge that just about every homegrown Japan international faces. top.title: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez is quietly having a Pro Bowl year
top.description: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team , the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams . And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati Bengals, twice. RELATED: BOJORQUEZ INTERVIEW Consider the fact that there aren’t any really good teams left on their schedule. Could they still make the playoffs? A division title seems out of reach, but it takes 10 or 11 wins to get that #7 seed, and they are already halfway to that goal. There are several players on the Browns roster who are having a good year. Guys like TE Harold Fannin, LBs Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, plus DT Mason Graham are getting their fair share of press regarding possibly getting some major Pro Bowl votes. But one player stands out, and nobody is talking about his season: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. Bojo has quietly been killing it as Cleveland’s punter this season. He was re-signed during last March’s free agency period. Currently, he is listed #5 in the league in net average per punt with 44.0 yards. The league leader is just 46.1, so Bojorquez is keeping the rankings tight. He is ranked #4 in average distance per kick at 50.4. Again, the leader’s number is close at 51.8, so one game could alter these numbers. Usually, the punters with the most kicks in a season are on teams whose offensive units can’t finish drives, or are unable to sustain drives. Bojo is ranked #3 in the most punts with 43. The league leader plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, which backs up this stat goes to guys who are on struggling offensive teams. He booted a season-high eight punts in the loss to the New York Jets when the offense could not move the ball. Bojo is considered a field flipper . This means his kicks can alter the opposing team’s field position just off one punt that has traveled 50+ yards. Case in point, in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, Bojorquez’s first punt was for 68 yards. Pretty good, eh? His first punt of the second half was 60 yards. Then his final kick was for a whopping 81 yards that went from Cleveland’s 19-yard line into the end zone. top.title: Valentino Rossi in new autobiography: '2015 still hurts, Marc Marquez wanted me to lose'
top.description: Motorsport photo Valentino Rossi has revisited his 2015 feud with Marc Marquez in his new autobiography, maintaining that the Spaniard interfered in his MotoGP title battle with Jorge Lorenzo . The nine-time world champion previously published a book about his career while he was still at the peak of his powers. But a new work, La Mia Storia , will be released on 10 November, offering a fresh account of the defining moments of a legendary and often controversial career. Although 11 years have passed, the events of the 2015 Malaysian Grand Prix remain a defining chapter in the Italian's life. Rossi was fighting Lorenzo for what would have been his 10th world title and arrived at Sepang accusing Marquez, with whom he had already been involved in several contentious incidents in Argentina and Assen that year, of conspiring to ensure a Spanish rider won the MotoGP championship. Marquez responded with an uncompromising battle during Sunday's race, which culminated in the infamous clash in which Rossi appeared to kick the Honda rider off his bike. Rossi believed Marquez, who was already out of title contention, was solely intent on losing him the championship. Rossi was subsequently penalised with a back-of-the-grid start in the Valencia finale, where tensions reached unprecedented levels between the three protagonists and among the fans who had travelled to the circuit. The race attracted record television audiences worldwide and ended with Lorenzo being crowned champion, while Rossi accused Marquez of a 'biscotto' – an alleged agreement to avoid attacking Lorenzo and prevent the title from going to the Italian. Rossi appeared on RAI's Che tempo che fa programme on Sunday to promote his new autobiography, which looks back on his sporting career. Inevitably, the interviewer asked him about the events of 2015. Rossi insisted that his version of events had not changed, admitting that what happened still hurts and that he regrets how much attention is devoted to the title he lost rather than the championships he won. top.title: Bryson DeChambeau Speaks As LIV Golf Files For Bankruptcy
top.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Bryson DeChambeau has confirmed his exit from LIV Golf as the league files for bankruptcy and scraps plans for a reboot. Lawyers representing the company told a New Jersey court on Thursday that the tour will wind down operations and enter liquidation. The move ends years of speculation about a second version of the breakaway circuit. DeChambeau posted a statement on X on Sunday, thanking fans and staff while refusing to change his past actions. To commit to the 2027 DP World Tour season, the American golfer must declare his intention by November 15. If he misses this deadline, he risks being frozen out of professional golf entirely. This timeline comes after the Saudi Public Investment Fund stopped its $5 billion support in April. BC Partners had pledged $300 million to back a new launch, but the firm pulled out when players did not sign on in time. A Statement on Four Years DeChambeau defended his choice to leave the PGA Tour and join LIV from the start. He thanked the staff, caddies, and operations crews who bet their careers on the new league. “I’m not going to rewrite the last four years,” DeChambeau wrote, according to Sky Sports . He noted that the record crowds in Adelaide and Johannesburg would stick with him for the rest of his life. He believes the game could reach more people in new ways, and he still holds that view. The former U.S. Open champion gave everything he had to keep team golf alive. He thanked his Crushers GC teammates and sponsors for their support. Despite the liquidation, he remained quiet about his own future plans. Arnold Palmer stated that no player is bigger than the game, according to his acknowledgment. DeChambeau admitted he said some things that did not help along the way and promised to move forward with humility. The Path Back to the Tour The PGA Tour will not reopen its Returning Member Program to let LIV players back in easily. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp stated earlier this year that the tour is a membership organization with strict rules. “The tour is a membership organization,” Rolapp said, according to AOL.com . He noted that rules only matter if they are enforced, and accountability is essential for the integrity of the game. A public decision on a return pathway is not expected until at least January. Adam Scott expressed a clear view on how former LIV golfers should return to the main circuit. He contended that athletes must earn their place in any system they choose to join. “I think the fairest thing is that they all re-establish themselves in the system that they want to go to,” Scott told Today’s Golfer. Although Jon Rahm was a major circuit name with an initial return path, he closed that door. DeChambeau confirmed he will compete in December at the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa. top.title: 2027: Nnaji vows to end excessive taxation in Enugu
top.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has said he is contesting the 2027 election to rescue the state from what he described as excessive taxation and its impact on businesses and residents. Nnaji alleged that the high tax burden was forcing businessmen and investors to relocate from the state, adding that Enugu had become one of the most expensive places to do business in the country. He spoke while addressing indigenes of Enugu State resident in Aba, Abia State, under the umbrella of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Abia State chapter. The former Minister of Science and Technology pledged to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, job creation and measures to address insecurity and unemployment. He said he had been consulting Enugu indigenes living outside the state to draw their attention to what he described as the challenges facing the state and seek their support ahead of the election. Nnaji expressed concern over what he described as the return of armed robbery in parts of Enugu, attributing the development to unemployment, hunger and economic hardship. He promised to establish industries that would create employment opportunities, reduce poverty and take more than 50,000 youths off the streets. “What is happening in Enugu State is condemnable. Enugu is for all, but today, businessmen and investors are relocating from the state due to excessive taxation. And the state government doesn’t care. “Our people are suffering from excessive taxation, even in the rural areas. Traders in rural communities only open their businesses in the evening when tax officials have left. Government collects N36,000 from traders in the villages, when most of them do not make such an amount annually. “Tax is based on profit, not on shops, as they are doing in Enugu. People are hungry. Armed people now invade homes at midnight to collect phones, computers and food items such as rice, beans and garri. This is something that happened more than 20 years ago,” he said. The PDP candidate also questioned the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), claiming that it had risen from N26 billion to N406.7 billion. He compared the figure with the revenue generated by Abia and Anambra states, arguing that the high revenue collection raised questions about the state’s taxation policies and their impact on businesses. Nnaji further alleged that Enugu’s debt profile had increased significantly under the current administration, although he did not provide figures to substantiate the claim. He said government should focus on creating wealth and improving the living conditions of residents rather than imposing taxes that could undermine businesses. “We have set up the Enugu State Recovery Committee, with me as chairman. top.title: The Lakers' continue to have one big problem despite their success
top.description: The Los Angeles Lakers have a 10-2 record after downing the Atlanta Hawks 124-114 on Monday despite being without Austin Reaves, who sat out due to an illness. They now have the best record in the NBA, as well as the league's highest scoring average, offensive rating and overall field-goal accuracy. But there still seems to be the suspicion across the league that the Lakers aren't a championship-caliber team. While L.A. has defeated teams with good records such as the Hawks, Detroit Pistons , Golden State Warriors and Portland Trail Blazers , it still has issues that have to be sorted out before it gets to the next level. Los Angeles doesn't have a legitimate third scoring option alongside Reaves and Luka Doncic in the starting lineup. It also ranks 19th in defensive rating, although it is second in opponents' turnover percentage and first in points off turnovers per game. But the Lakers continue to have another weakness that has plagued them over the last few years, and it is one that will hurt them when they play against true contenders, as well as during the playoffs. L.A. is still weak on the boards Over the last few years, the Lakers have had problems in the rebounding department, and in the early going of this season, those problems have continued. Through Monday, they're 22nd in rebounding percentage and 28th in defensive rebounding percentage. While they have improved to 15th in offensive rebounding percentage, they continue to get outrebounded or merely play their opponents to a relative draw in the rebounding department on a regular basis. Los Angeles is 28th in the league in opponents' second-chance points per game. The team continues to be weak in all these areas even though new center Walker Kessler has been as good as advertised. He's averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 boards, 2.3 blocks and 1.3 steals in 30.9 minutes a game. A big reason for this lack of rebounding is the fact that the Lakers simply lack forwards who are strong on the boards, as well as a competent backup center. They have been using Sandro Mamukelashvili, who is 6-foot-10 and 240 pounds, as a backup center, and while he's a decent rebounder, he also isn't a force in that category. Other than Kessler and Doncic, none of the Lakers' regular rotation players average over seven rebounds per 36 minutes. Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Ziaire Williams, who have started games at forward this season, are underwhelming rebounders. Forward Jarred Vanderbilt is capable of getting rebounds in bunches, but due to his extreme limitations on offense, he doesn't receive and shouldn't receive more than spot-duty minutes. The only real way for the Lakers to rectify this lack of rebounding is to make a trade, but that will take a while. The NBA's trade market historically doesn't heat up until after Dec. 15, which is the earliest date that players signed as free agents during that year's offseason can be traded. Until then, L.A. will have to find other ways to win the possession battle

top.title: Watch: Alejandro Balde left surprised as Flick decided to bring De Jong at right-back against Atletico Madrid
top.description: Watch: Alejandro Balde left surprised as Flick decided to bring De Jong at right-back against Atletico Madrid Alejandro Balde’s reaction to Hansi Flick’s unexpected decision to deploy Frenkie de Jong at right-back against Atletico Madrid offered another glimpse into the Barcelona defender’s uncertain position under the German coach. As De Jong learned about his new role during the half-time team talk, Balde watched the conversation closely, appearing serious as the tactical change was explained. The moment was particularly notable because Balde is a natural left-back who has struggled to secure regular minutes this season. With Joao Cancelo capable of playing on either flank, Flick could have made a conventional defensive adjustment by moving the Portuguese defender to the right and introducing Balde on the left. Instead, he chose De Jong , leaving the Spaniard on the bench. Balde watches as Flick turns to De Jong Broadcast footage captured the reactions on the Barcelona bench when the coaching staff informed De Jong that he would be playing at right-back. The Dutchman initially appeared surprised but accepted the instruction, later explaining the change to teammates Gavi and Wojciech Szczesny. Balde was also listening attentively as the decision became clear. His reaction stood out because the situation could have presented a possible opportunity for him to enter the game, yet Flick opted for a midfielder who had previously filled the centre-back role. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The decision also needs to be viewed against Balde’s recent lack of involvement. Joao Cancelo has become Flick’s preferred option at left-back after Xavi Espart’s injury, while the Spaniard has struggled to establish himself in the starting XI. As a result, his situation has attracted attention in the transfer market, and on that note, we have reported earlier that Balde is open to a January departure if it offers him the opportunity to play regularly and rebuild his confidence, and he certainly does not lack suitors. nigeria.title: 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway pileup
nigeria.description: Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU. Crashes in thick fog snared dozens of vehicles heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas. An estimated 50 cars and trucks were involved in the accident near the city of Yambol, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency, as government officials rushed to the scene. Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles. “The toll at this point is 11 dead and 48 injured,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters. Radev was meeting EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, who is on a visit to Bulgaria, but the prime minister cancelled his official events scheduled for later Tuesday. The injured were transported to hospitals in nearby cities. The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams. Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures. Victims blame the Balkan nation’s high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system. Stricter penalties Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed “deepest condolences” to the victims and their families in a post on X. European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was “deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning”. A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 — down five percent from the previous year and 27 percent lower than in 2019. The EU in 2019 introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 percent by 2030. A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains “one of the world’s safest regions for road travel”, the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target. The report said that just five of the EU’s 27 countries — including Bulgaria — were on track to meet the target. However, “despite their progress since 2019, Bulgaria and Romania, alongside Croatia, continue to have the highest fatality rates in the EU when measuring deaths per million inhabitants”, the report said. In 2023, Bulgaria’s parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs. The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record. Bulgaria’s busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts. nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has disclosed that less than 36 per cent of Nigerians have access to improved toilet facilities, raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges and the associated public health risks. The Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, disclosed this on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day. Lawal, who was represented by the Director of Pollution Control and Environmental Health, Mrs Omotunde Adeola, said many public places, including markets, motor parks, schools and communities, still lacked adequate and functional toilet facilities. He warned that the situation was contributing to open defecation, contamination of food and water sources, and the spread of sanitation-related diseases such as cholera and typhoid. According to him, inadequate sanitation poses serious threats to public health, environmental safety and human dignity. The minister said women, girls, children, older persons and persons living with disabilities were particularly affected by the shortage of appropriate sanitation facilities. He stressed that no child should miss school because of inadequate toilet facilities, while no woman or girl should be forced to compromise her safety and dignity because of the absence of suitable toilets. Providing a global perspective, Lawal said about 4.5 billion people worldwide still lacked safely managed sanitation, while 892 million continued to practise open defecation. He said the figures underscored the need to accelerate efforts towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those relating to clean water and sanitation, gender equality, good health and sustainable communities by 2030. Government interventions On efforts to address the challenge, the minister said the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with relevant ministries, state governments and development partners, was implementing programmes to improve sanitation and promote safe excreta disposal nationwide. He listed the initiatives to include capacity building for Environmental Health Officers on faecal sludge management and toilet design, the Clean and Green Programme, and the Community-Based Waste Management and Open Defecation Control Programme. Other interventions, he said, included integrating sanitation into climate adaptation and circular economy initiatives, as well as partnering with private sector operators to provide environmentally friendly sanitation facilities. Lawal announced that the ministry would convene a National Dialogue on Faecal Sludge Management on November 23, 2026, involving seven selected states across the six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the dialogue would enable participating states to assess their experiences, share challenges and develop practical recommendations for improving faecal sludge management. nigeria.title: Troops rescue three kidnap victims, kill two terrorists in Adamawa
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK) have rescued three kidnapped civilians and killed two terrorists in separate operations in Adamawa State. The troops also recovered two AK-47 rifles, ammunition, locally fabricated explosive devices, stolen vehicles and farm produce belonging to residents who narrowly escaped abduction. The Acting Media Information Officer of OPHK, Capt. Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday. He said the three victims were rescued by troops deployed in Mubi following a distress call from farmers around Dutse-Uku in Mubi South Local Government Area. According to him, suspected kidnappers abducted a farmer, identified as Happiness Dama Dauda, on November 9 while she was working on her farm and also stole her motorcycle. Goni said the troops, working with local hunters, mobilised to the area and mounted pressure on the kidnappers, forcing them to abandon their victim and flee. He added that a sustained pursuit led to the rescue of two other residents suspected to have been abducted earlier, bringing the number of rescued victims to three. The troops also recovered a motorcycle, a tricycle conveying 15 bags of beans and a Hi-Jet pickup carrying 13 bags of groundnuts belonging to other farmers who narrowly escaped abduction. Goni said the respective village heads identified the recovered items, which were subsequently handed over to their owners. Two terrorists killed in Gombi In a separate operation on November 8, troops deployed at Zangula Kilba Junction in Gombi Local Government Area foiled an attempted attack by suspected Boko Haram/Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists. Two terrorists were killed during the encounter, while others fled following what the military described as the troops’ superior combat readiness and tactical resilience. Items recovered from the fleeing insurgents included two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 115 rounds of ammunition, three belts of empty ammunition links and two cases of locally fabricated explosive devices. Other recovered items included a pair of desert boots, a backpack, an Android phone, a wristwatch and N15,000. Goni said troops had commenced exploitation operations to track down the fleeing terrorists and prevent them from regrouping. He added that troops were maintaining aggressive patrols and surveillance across the affected areas to prevent further attacks and reassure residents of their safety. The military urged residents to provide timely and credible intelligence to security agencies, stressing that collaboration between troops and local communities remained critical to tackling terrorism and other security threats. Operation Hadin Kai reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining operational pressure on terrorists and their collaborators to deny them the freedom to threaten the security and livelihoods of residents across the North-East. nigeria.title: Madonna University: 15 nursing students beg for expulsion reversal over TikTok video
nigeria.description: By Chioma Okoye Fifteen nursing students of Madonna University, Nigeria, have appealed to the university management to reverse their expulsion over a controversial TikTok video recorded during their community posting, pleading for another opportunity to complete their studies. The students, in a letter dated November 2, 2026, tendered an unreserved apology to the management, admitting that their conduct was unethical and had brought disrepute to the nursing profession and the university community. The video, which went viral on social media, sparked widespread reactions and prompted disciplinary action by the university management. In the appeal addressed to the university management through the Registrar, the students said they had reflected deeply on their actions and were genuinely remorseful. “We sincerely regret our said actions and assure the University Management and all relevant authorities that such an incident will not repeat itself again,” they said. They pleaded with the management to reconsider its decision, stressing that their families had made significant sacrifices to support their education and enable them to reach the present stage of their academic journey. The students said reversing the expulsion would give them an opportunity to complete their programmes and pursue their chosen professional careers instead of having their academic aspirations cut short. They also appreciated the university management for engaging with their parents and guardians and allowing them to present their concerns. According to the students, they did not take the gesture for granted and remained grateful for the opportunity given to their families to be heard. The appeal, jointly signed by the 15 students, urged the university management to reconsider the punishment and give them a second chance. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s achievements will make it difficult to unseat him – Wike
nigeria.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says it will be immensely difficult for opposition parties to unseat President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. Wike said this in Abuja on Tuesday, after inspecting some ongoing projects within the federal capital territory. He cited what he described as Tinubu’s undeniable and rich report card of infrastructure development across the country. The minister said that the volume and pace of visible achievements delivered under Tinubu’s administration left very little room for political detractors to challenge the ruling party’s record. “You can see clearly that it will be difficult to unseat the president today because the report card is obvious in terms of what he has done. “Like I told you, this is our campaign. People ask what we are going to campaign with, but we have so many visible achievements all around us. “There is no way residents of Abuja will see the kind of infrastructure we have provided and say they are not happy with the achievements of Mr President. It is second to none,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the minister inspected the ongoing construction of Innet Southern Motorway, from the Area 1 roundabout to the Games Village bridges and Southern Parkway, linking Oladipo Diya Road with Ring Road II. He also inspected the ongoing construction of the Arterial Road S1 project in Abuja to connect Ring Road II to the FCT Fire Service Station in the Kaura and Gaduwa district corridors. Highlighting the rapid speed of execution on several key projects in the territory, Wike referenced the rapid transformation of the Southern Parkway project, which was flagged during the celebration of Tinubu’s third year in office. “Within six to seven months, you can see what has been achieved. “It is unimaginable, and that is why we are very happy,” Wike said. He pledged that the FCT administration remained on track to inaugurate at least 10 high-impact projects before the general elections scheduled for Jan. 16, 2027. nigeria.title: Zamfara APC crisis deepens as aspirant petitions NEC, security agencies
nigeria.description: …Yilwatda dismisses allegations as unfounded By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The crisis in the Zamfara State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has taken a fresh turn, following a petition by an aspirant to the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), National Working Committee (NWC) and security agencies over the composition of a committee to conduct a court-ordered fresh primary election. The primary is for the Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency following an order by the Court of Appeal. The aspirant, Honourable Hassan Umar Dangaladima, accused the party’s National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, of unilaterally constituting the committee without involving the NWC. He alleged that the committee’s composition raised concerns about its impartiality and called on the party leadership to review the arrangement before the fresh primary. In the petition, Dangaladima claimed that no NWC meeting was convened to deliberate on or approve the committee’s composition and that neither the aspirants nor the Zamfara State chapter and other relevant stakeholders were consulted. However, Yilwatda, through his Special Adviser on Media and Strategic Communication, Abimbola Tooki, dismissed the allegations as unfounded. He said the claims did not reflect the party’s established decision-making process, insisting that the NWC operated as a collective body. “The National Chairman does not operate in isolation. He works in consultation and collaboration with other members of the NWC, and decisions are taken collectively in accordance with the party’s constitution, established procedures and internal mechanisms,” Tooki said. He described the suggestion that Yilwatda single-handedly constituted the committee without the knowledge or involvement of the NWC as misleading. According to him, the APC remains committed to respecting the rule of law, implementing court directives and ensuring that its internal processes are transparent, fair and credible. “The APC is a democratic institution governed by rules and collective responsibility, not the personal preferences of any individual,” he said. Alleges committee bias Dangaladima, however, maintained that the committee’s composition raised concerns about a possible conflict of interest. He alleged that some members were loyalists, supporters or agents of another aspirant, Honourable Aminu Sani Jaji, whom he described as his main rival in the contest. The petitioner also challenged Jaji’s eligibility, alleging that his name was not contained in the APC membership register for Birnin Magaji Ward submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said he obtained a Certified True Copy of the register from INEC, which he attached to his petition as evidence. nigeria.title: Gombe records 98 road crash deaths, 1,345 injuries in nine months — FRSC
nigeria.description: By Ben Ngwakwe GOMBE — The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has disclosed that 98 persons were killed while 1,345 others sustained injuries in road traffic crashes recorded across Gombe State between January and September 2026. The FRSC Sector Commander in the state, Commander Samson Kaura, disclosed this on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing members of the Gombe State Council of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) during the commemoration of the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. Kaura said the command recorded 1,345 road traffic incidents during the nine-month period, adding that fatalities increased by six per cent compared with the corresponding period. He identified excessive speeding and reckless driving as major causes of road crashes and fatalities, warning that irresponsible road use continued to pose a serious threat to motorists and other road users. According to him, the annual World Day of Remembrance provides an opportunity to honour those who have lost their lives or sustained serious injuries in road crashes, while drawing attention to the need for stronger legal responses to traffic offences resulting in deaths and injuries. He said the commemoration also seeks to promote better support for crash victims and their families, as well as evidence-based interventions to prevent and ultimately eliminate road traffic deaths and injuries. The sector commander expressed concern that the fatalities recorded in the first nine months of 2026 had surpassed the figure for the whole of 2025. He said the command recorded 1,614 road traffic incidents in 2025, resulting in 92 deaths and 926 injuries. Kaura described the 2026 World Day of Remembrance as a campaign aimed at translating remembrance into concrete action, stressing the need for collective responsibility in addressing road traffic crashes. In his response, the Vice Chairman of the Gombe State NUJ Council, Emmanuel Akila, who represented the state chairman, Faruk Muazu Gombe, pledged the union’s continued cooperation with the FRSC in promoting road safety and development. Akila, however, urged the FRSC to strengthen collaboration with the union to identify and curb the activities of fake journalists in the state. He called on the corps to insist on proper identification of journalists during official engagements and other road-related activities to prevent impersonation and protect the integrity of the journalism profession. The NUJ vice chairman also urged the FRSC to intensify enforcement against vehicle overloading, describing the practice as one of the factors contributing to fatalities in road crashes. He stressed the need for sustained public enlightenment, effective enforcement of traffic regulations and stronger collaboration among relevant stakeholders to reduce road crashes and safeguard lives on the highways. nigeria.title: UK, Nigeria seal $750m infrastructure deal as Pension funds prepare to unlock billions

The initiative, which has already attracted interest from 19 Nigerian pension funds, is expected to channel long-term domestic and international investments into key sectors, including energy, transportation and digital infrastructure, as both countries seek to address the continent’s widening infrastructure financing gap. A statement from PenCom disclosed that the agreement was signed by Nigeria’s Pension Industry Leadership Council, PILC,and UK-funded specialist development agency, FSD Africa, in Lagos on November 10, 2026. Under the agreement, FSD Africa will provide technical expertise and advisory support to PILC towards establishing the proposed investment platform, including the selection of a fund manager through a competitive process, engagement with prospective investors and development finance institutions, capacity building and support for necessary regulatory reforms. The initiative was developed by Nigerian Pension Fund Administrators, PFAs, with support from the National Pension Commission, PenCom, and FSD Africa. Speaking on the development, UK Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Jonny Baxter, said the partnership reflected the shared commitment of both countries to mobilising domestic capital, particularly pension funds, for productive investment in the real economy. According to him: “The UK is proud to partner with the Nigeria’s Pension Industry and the pensions regulator Pencom to progress this investment. Both our countries are prioritising tacking the challenge of attracting more domestic capital, including from pension funds, into the real economy. nigeria.title: Ologe highlights growing importance of risk leadership in digital business
nigeria.description: Mojisola Ologe, an Associate Chartered Risk Manager, has highlighted the growing importance of risk management in strengthening corporate governance, business performance and operational resilience amid increasing digitalisation. Ologe, who received the professional designation from the Chartered Risk Management Institute of Nigeria (CRMI) on October 15, 2026, said effective risk management was becoming increasingly important as organisations expanded their reliance on technology and digital services. She noted that decisions involving access to information systems, introduction of new services, third-party dependencies and business recovery arrangements could have direct implications for customers, regulatory compliance and organisational credibility. Her professional experience spans consulting, banking and digital payments, including roles at Phillips Consulting and Sterling Bank, where she worked across technology assurance, information technology risk and control, business continuity and compliance oversight. The experience, according to her, has reinforced the need to translate identified operational and technological weaknesses into practical business implications and corrective actions. Ologe currently serves as Chief Risk and Compliance Officer at Hydrogen Payment Services Limited, where her responsibilities cover enterprise risk management, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity governance and operational resilience. In the digital payments sector, these areas are closely interconnected, as disruptions to technology systems can quickly affect customer services, expose businesses to financial losses and create regulatory challenges. Effective risk management, therefore, goes beyond identifying potential threats to understanding business operations, assessing critical dependencies and ensuring that management takes timely corrective action. Clear accountability, appropriate internal controls and effective escalation mechanisms are also essential to helping organisations address vulnerabilities while pursuing their business objectives. Ologe’s professional recognition by CRMI underscores the importance of continuous professional development in the risk management sector, particularly as emerging technologies and changing business conditions create new operational and regulatory challenges. Risk professionals, increasingly, are expected to contribute beyond compliance monitoring by providing insights that inform corporate strategy, investment decisions and everyday business operations. Their role, the profile noted, is to help organisations pursue growth while maintaining a clear understanding of potential exposures and strengthening their capacity to withstand disruptions. nigeria.title: US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The United States House of Representatives is set to hold a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s efforts to protect Christians and tackle insecurity in the Middle Belt, with Republican lawmaker Chris Smith leading the session on Thursday, November 12. According to a statement issued by Smith’s office on Monday, the session is titled ‘One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt’, with hearing scheduled for 11am at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, DC. It partly reads, “Congressional hearing that assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities; and the steps the United States can take to ensure that Nigerian officials are addressing and preventing the systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.” The first panel will feature Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, and Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour. The second panel will include Nina Shea, senior fellow and director of the Centre for Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute; Ryan Brown, chief executive officer of Open Doors US; and Oge Onubogu, director and senior fellow of the Africa Programme at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. The hearing will be streamed live on YouTube. This will be Smith’s 14th congressional hearing exclusively on Nigeria. In November 2025, he chaired a hearing after President Donald Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a ‘country of particular concern’. nigeria.title: Carrick set to be sacked by Man Utd: reports
nigeria.description: Michael Carrick is set to be sacked by Manchester United after his side’s dismal start to the season, according to reports on Tuesday. United’s hierarchy have been conducting an internal review of the club’s miserable form and it is believed that Carrick will shortly be relieved of his duties. United are in the midst of their worst opening to a campaign in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. Although it is said that no final decision has been made, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United owners the Glazer family and influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe would then decide whether to act on that recommendation. Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training base on Tuesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old, hired on a permanent basis in the close season after a successful interim spell last term, had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. United’s surprise decision to let Carrick limp on failed to produce a significant improvement in performances, particularly defensively. They were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It looked certain that former United midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But United’s powerbrokers look set to make yet another managerial change in a bid to avoid being dragged into an embarrassing relegation battle. USA boss Mauricio Pochettino, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to secure a replacement for Carrick before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. nigeria.title: Wenger considers challenging Infantino for FIFA presidency — Report
nigeria.description: Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering a challenge against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, according to the BBC. The 77-year-old Frenchman is giving serious thought to contesting the position following growing calls from influential figures in European football for him to enter the race. Some of Wenger’s supporters have reportedly indicated that they would back him even if he chose to step down before completing the four-year presidential term. His possible candidacy could pose a significant challenge to Infantino, whose leadership has faced criticism following the collapse of a plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Although the controversy has unsettled his position in parts of European football, Infantino retains considerable support in South America, Africa and Asia. He recently maintained that he enjoys the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of the global football community. Wenger, who currently serves as Fifa’s Chief of Global Football Development, is expected to enjoy the backing of the Union of European Football Associations (Uefa), which has led opposition to Infantino over the abandoned commercial proposal. However, sources close to the Frenchman told BBC Sport that he has yet to make a final decision on whether to contest the election. They also believe Infantino remains the favourite to secure another term. The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to challenge Infantino is November 18, ahead of the election scheduled for March. Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega became the first candidate to announce his intention to run in October, while Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also indicated interest in the position. nigeria.title: US Judge Orders Psychiatric Exam For Meghan Markle’s Father
nigeria.description: A US judge has ordered a psychiatric examination for Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Prince Harry’s wife, Meghan Markle, after his arrest for alleged possession of images of child sexual abuse. Thomas Markle, 82, is charged with one count of “possession of child pornography” and made an initial court appearance in Tampa in Florida on Friday. Judge Lindsay Griffin cited his “health condition,” “advanced age” and “lack of recall” in the order issued on Friday, without providing further details. Markle was taken into custody by FBI agents earlier that day at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida. The Justice Department said he allegedly “kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades.” File photo of Meghan and Thomas Markle Pictures of child sex abuse have also allegedly been found at Markle’s former home in the Philippines and at a storage unit he rented in Mexico. The judge said she found “reasonable cause to believe” that Markle was suffering from a condition “rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense.” She instructed a psychiatrist to provide a report on Markle’s mental state by November 20. The judge permitted Markle to be moved to house arrest with electronic monitoring, CNN reported. Markle had been living in Cebu in the Philippines until reportedly returning to the United States this year. Meghan Markle said last month that she was “deeply distressed” by accusations that her father possessed images of child sexual abuse. He could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. Show commitment. Demonstrate that you really mean what you are talking about. When you win, come, and we are going to reward you,” he said. Wike spoke on Tuesday during an inspection of ongoing infrastructure projects in Abuja. He was responding to criticism of the promise, which he said was an incentive for hard work and not an attempt to buy votes. Addressing stakeholders, traditional leaders, and political actors in Kwali Area Council the previous day, Wike had explained that the initiative was part of a broad grassroots mobilisation strategy designed to rally maximum support at the grassroots level. “For the councillors, you have a task. I will hold a meeting with you again, and I will now say the way I am going to mobilise you, but I will give you a bet, like what is happening in the stars; it’s a competition. “Anybody who delivers his ward, if you deliver your ward, that is what the Rainbow Coalition has decided to do as mobilisation and support for Mr President; we have to start in the FCT (I couldn’t say so when the president came because they gave me only two minutes to talk). But now that I have time to talk, let me say that the Rainbow Coalition all over the federation, as a form of mobilisation for Mr President to win this election, is saying that any councillor that delivers his ward will come and take N10 million. We want to mobilise for Mr President. So, go to your wards, and go and see your leaders. I know only you cannot do it, but we are using you as an instrumentality for your leaders. Go and meet your leaders and say, ‘Look, oh, there is something that has come.’ We must not allow this thing to go. Let’s dedicate our ward for Mr President’. So, that is for that,” Wike had said. Speaking on Tuesday, Wike drew a line between rewarding political commitment and offering money to voters in exchange for their support. He said the councillors were challenged to prove their commitment through effective mobilisation. Political parties and candidates, he argued, routinely spend money on campaign advertisements without facing the same scrutiny. nigeria.title: French Students Block Dozens Of Schools
nigeria.description: French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, the education ministry said, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions. Student protests across France since September have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by fringe violence and accusations of police brutality. The unrest comes ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron next year. With the European Union’s second biggest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Students dance in front of police officers during a rally over learning conditions as part of a nationwide day of action, as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Paris on November 5, 2026. Forty-nine of the country’s 3,700 high schools for 15- to 18-year-olds were blockaded on Tuesday morning, the ministry said. Authorities expected several thousand school and university students at a Paris protest on Tuesday afternoon. “Now is the time to step up the mobilisation by continuing to put pressure on the government,” student and teacher unions said in a joint statement released Monday. Student association leader Ryad Rani said it was essential to keep up the pressure. “We’re not just fighting for ourselves. We’re fighting for teachers, for their working conditions,” he said. The government has announced measures including the gradual replacement of an online selection platform to access higher education, as well as financial means for some of the worst-off schools. But students say this is not enough. Unions are not happy either, with one leader saying on Monday that a government pledge to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent on top of a standard adjustment for inflation was “crumbs”. They have called for a new day of strikes and protests on November 17. Around 575,000 people demonstrated across the country during cost-of-living strikes and protests last Thursday, according to authorities. Unions put the number at 1.5 million. business.title: Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide Amundi, Europe’s largest asset manager, raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by about 44% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 6 shows, lifting the position to 1,903,725 shares worth $291.4 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 579,672 shares from the 1,324,053 Amundi reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $115.1 million. The Paris-based firm managed €2.579 trillion in assets at the end of September, up 11% year over year, and described itself as Europe’s leading asset manager. The filing lands as MSTR has given back much of its third-quarter run. Strategy shares closed at $153.09 on Sept. 30 and near $126 on Monday, an 18% drop that would put Amundi’s disclosed stake near $239 million at the latest close, Yahoo Finance data show. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. Amundi filed a combination report that folds in 17 other managers across its group, so the Strategy line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. Strategy keeps buying while the stock slides Strategy itself kept stacking. The company bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week for $81.9 million at an average of $79,012, a Monday 8-K filing and company release show, lifting its treasury to 850,364 BTC acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456. That average cost now sits above the spot bitcoin price, leaving the stack underwater on paper even after the firm added 811 bitcoin the prior week. Strategy’s public ledger still ranks it as the largest corporate bitcoin holder, with the stack equal to roughly 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. MSTR roughly doubled during the third quarter itself. The June 30 13F valued Amundi’s then-smaller stake at an implied $86.93 a share, against the $153.09 Sept. 30 close, so the dollar value of the position rose faster than the share count. Since then the stock has tracked bitcoin’s slide into the mid-$70,000s, wiping out a large share of that mark-to-market gain for anyone still holding the Sept. 30 position. The timing matters because Strategy funds most of its bitcoin buys by selling new MSTR common under an at-the-market program. A weaker share price raises more dilution for every coin purchased, which is the feedback loop that has defined the stock’s moves this year. Banks loaded bitcoin proxies in the same quarter Amundi was not the only large European name adding bitcoin exposure on the quarter. Punchbowl published the aide’s rundown of her agenda on Monday. Warren intends to use the committee’s investigative powers for oversight of prediction markets and election betting platforms, aimed at insider trading and platform manipulation — the same fight she opened before the midterms. That earlier push was bipartisan. On Oct. 28, Warren and Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, wrote to Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour and Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan asking how the companies stop candidates, campaign staff and others with material nonpublic information from trading election contracts. It also referenced an NPR investigation of campaign insiders who said they traded ahead of polling releases. “The identification of isolated instances of improper trading does not demonstrate that these markets are adequately protected,” Warren and Curtis wrote . “Instead, it raises serious questions about how much similar activity may be going undetected.” They asked for written answers by Election Day, Nov. 3. entertainment.title: 5 New Albums to Listen to This Week: Skepta, Phyno, Ty Bello & More
entertainment.description: Skepta holding the official clear vinyl edition of his sixth studio album, The Fork and Knife. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. sports.title: The strange reason Japan can’t pick their best fly half against England
sports.description: In the aftermath of his side’s defeat to Wales, the Japan head coach Eddie Jones already had more than half an eye on England . “We’ll need to be able to break up the game,” the veteran schemer said with a glint in his eye and a familiar smirk on his face. “If we play an orthodox game of rugby, we’re probably going to struggle to beat them. And the English don’t react well to unorthodox rugby. We’ve got to think about how we can play quite unorthodoxly.” Jones speaks, of course, from experience. It was his England side that were baffled by Italy’s radical ruck tactics in the Six Nations in 2017 ; in a neat twist, Conor O’Shea, the architect of that plan, now heads up performance at England’s Rugby Football Union (RFU). “Maybe we’ll play like Italy did in 2017,” Jones teased. “Can you still play like that in the rucks? I don’t think you can, can you?” Eddie Jones has promised to throw a few curveballs at England (Getty) England are bracing for something similarly avant-garde nonetheless. It is instructive, though, that Jones is having to talk in such terms about a side he does not yet see as an equal to the world’s top teams. Japan beat Italy and pushed Ireland close in July, before coming within three points of Australia in August – they have the talent to at least give England a fright. There is one key difference from those games, though. In each of those encounters, Japan were steered from fly half by Ryunosuke Ito, a 21-year-old playmaker long tipped for a bright future who was named to start against France before he had even played a senior club game. He took to Test rugby like a natural; through the Nations Championship, Australia series and Pacific Nations Cup, the No 10 shirt was his. For a team that had struggled to replace Yu Tamura, and with Lee Seung Sin injured, here was the welcome emergence of a new, young star. Ryunosuke Ito has emerged as a budding star for Japan (Getty) That flourishing has been brought to a strange and unwelcome halt, though. Ito is not in the United Kingdom with the rest of Jones’s squad, with Riku Kitahara steering the ship against Wales in Cardiff instead. Kitahara performed well; about as well as one might expect of a player reportedly described by Jones as his fourth-choice fly half. There is no injury to speak of to Ito. Why, then, is he absent? sports.description: Motorsport photo Valentino Rossi has revisited his 2015 feud with Marc Marquez in his new autobiography, maintaining that the Spaniard interfered in his MotoGP title battle with Jorge Lorenzo . The nine-time world champion previously published a book about his career while he was still at the peak of his powers. But a new work, La Mia Storia , will be released on 10 November, offering a fresh account of the defining moments of a legendary and often controversial career. Although 11 years have passed, the events of the 2015 Malaysian Grand Prix remain a defining chapter in the Italian's life. Rossi was fighting Lorenzo for what would have been his 10th world title and arrived at Sepang accusing Marquez, with whom he had already been involved in several contentious incidents in Argentina and Assen that year, of conspiring to ensure a Spanish rider won the MotoGP championship. Marquez responded with an uncompromising battle during Sunday's race, which culminated in the infamous clash in which Rossi appeared to kick the Honda rider off his bike. Rossi believed Marquez, who was already out of title contention, was solely intent on losing him the championship. Rossi was subsequently penalised with a back-of-the-grid start in the Valencia finale, where tensions reached unprecedented levels between the three protagonists and among the fans who had travelled to the circuit. The race attracted record television audiences worldwide and ended with Lorenzo being crowned champion, while Rossi accused Marquez of a 'biscotto' – an alleged agreement to avoid attacking Lorenzo and prevent the title from going to the Italian. Rossi appeared on RAI's Che tempo che fa programme on Sunday to promote his new autobiography, which looks back on his sporting career. Inevitably, the interviewer asked him about the events of 2015. Rossi insisted that his version of events had not changed, admitting that what happened still hurts and that he regrets how much attention is devoted to the title he lost rather than the championships he won. sports.title: The Lakers' continue to have one big problem despite their success
sports.description: The Los Angeles Lakers have a 10-2 record after downing the Atlanta Hawks 124-114 on Monday despite being without Austin Reaves, who sat out due to an illness. They now have the best record in the NBA, as well as the league's highest scoring average, offensive rating and overall field-goal accuracy. But there still seems to be the suspicion across the league that the Lakers aren't a championship-caliber team. While L.A. has defeated teams with good records such as the Hawks, Detroit Pistons , Golden State Warriors and Portland Trail Blazers , it still has issues that have to be sorted out before it gets to the next level. Los Angeles doesn't have a legitimate third scoring option alongside Reaves and Luka Doncic in the starting lineup. It also ranks 19th in defensive rating, although it is second in opponents' turnover percentage and first in points off turnovers per game. But the Lakers continue to have another weakness that has plagued them over the last few years, and it is one that will hurt them when they play against true contenders, as well as during the playoffs. L.A. is still weak on the boards Over the last few years, the Lakers have had problems in the rebounding department, and in the early going of this season, those problems have continued. Through Monday, they're 22nd in rebounding percentage and 28th in defensive rebounding percentage. While they have improved to 15th in offensive rebounding percentage, they continue to get outrebounded or merely play their opponents to a relative draw in the rebounding department on a regular basis. Los Angeles is 28th in the league in opponents' second-chance points per game. The team continues to be weak in all these areas even though new center Walker Kessler has been as good as advertised. He's averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 boards, 2.3 blocks and 1.3 steals in 30.9 minutes a game. A big reason for this lack of rebounding is the fact that the Lakers simply lack forwards who are strong on the boards, as well as a competent backup center. They have been using Sandro Mamukelashvili, who is 6-foot-10 and 240 pounds, as a backup center, and while he's a decent rebounder, he also isn't a force in that category. Other than Kessler and Doncic, none of the Lakers' regular rotation players average over seven rebounds per 36 minutes. Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Ziaire Williams, who have started games at forward this season, are underwhelming rebounders. Forward Jarred Vanderbilt is capable of getting rebounds in bunches, but due to his extreme limitations on offense, he doesn't receive and shouldn't receive more than spot-duty minutes. The only real way for the Lakers to rectify this lack of rebounding is to make a trade, but that will take a while. The NBA's trade market historically doesn't heat up until after Dec. 15, which is the earliest date that players signed as free agents during that year's offseason can be traded. Until then, L.A. will have to find other ways to win the possession battle

As De Jong learned about his new role during the half-time team talk, Balde watched the conversation closely, appearing serious as the tactical change was explained. The moment was particularly notable because Balde is a natural left-back who has struggled to secure regular minutes this season. With Joao Cancelo capable of playing on either flank, Flick could have made a conventional defensive adjustment by moving the Portuguese defender to the right and introducing Balde on the left. Instead, he chose De Jong , leaving the Spaniard on the bench. Balde watches as Flick turns to De Jong Broadcast footage captured the reactions on the Barcelona bench when the coaching staff informed De Jong that he would be playing at right-back. The Dutchman initially appeared surprised but accepted the instruction, later explaining the change to teammates Gavi and Wojciech Szczesny. Balde was also listening attentively as the decision became clear. His reaction stood out because the situation could have presented a possible opportunity for him to enter the game, yet Flick opted for a midfielder who had previously filled the centre-back role. It would be speculative to claim exactly what Balde was thinking, but what can be safely assumed is that he would not be entirely happy. Balde’s Barcelona situation remains uncertain De Jong played as a right-back against Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The decision also needs to be viewed against Balde’s recent lack of involvement. Joao Cancelo has become Flick’s preferred option at left-back after Xavi Espart’s injury, while the Spaniard has struggled to establish himself in the starting XI. technology.title: Ransomware threat blares from Vanderbilt University computers during cyberattack
technology.description: Classes at Vanderbilt University are proceeding as scheduled today, although access to most university systems remains restricted following a cyberattack claimed by ransomware group BYOD. Vanderbilt announced on Monday morning that it was dealing with "an active cybersecurity incident," and that the fallout may affect university devices, systems, and cloud-based services. The Nashville-based university initially told students and staff to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. It warned them to watch for unexpected prompts, altered files or permissions, unfamiliar applications, and unsolicited authentication requests. Campus computers reportedly began playing an audio threat attributed to BYOD. Student newspaper The Vanderbilt Hustler cited posts on campus social network Fizz showing the message. "You have been compromised by BYOD," the recording said. "We suggest you reach out to us as soon as possible. Instructions have been placed on your desktop. Failure to communicate will result in this estate being brought to the ground completely. Make the right choice or rot with the wrong one." By Monday evening, Vanderbilt had restored access to campus Wi-Fi, but warned that access to most systems remains restricted. "We know this has disrupted important work and caused frustration across the university," it said . "Vanderbilt Information Technology is working with government agencies and other partners to manage this situation." Students were told to attend classes as scheduled on Tuesday and contact instructors about flexibility on coursework deadlines. Staff were instructed to report to work normally. Vanderbilt's Athletics department said that its ticketing system was unavailable, and that students were unable to claim tickets for the college's football game against Alabama on Saturday. BYOD claimed responsibility for the attack on Vanderbilt on Monday, along with extensive data theft. "If you could not tell already, your databases are locked [and] we have your entire estate and research data," it said via its leak site. "Over 1 million SSNs, full names, email addresses, phone numbers, student and employee records, full takeover of your DC, whatever was on your network, we possess." Vanderbilt has not confirmed BYOD's claims about the extent of its access or the data allegedly stolen. BYOD may be a familiar name to some. The group previously claimed attacks on the University of New Mexico and Trump Mobile's customer database . BYOD also claimed responsibility on Monday for an attack on Texas Health and Human Services. The agency has not publicly confirmed an incident and did not immediately respond to our questions. ®

technology.title: Smart meters to cost the UK billions: 2G switch-off means replacing 12-13 million
technology.description: Between 12 and 13 million UK smart meters could stop working properly when 2G and 3G networks are switched off by 2033, and replacing them all is likely to cost around £4 billion ($5.3 billion). Smart meters have long been a controversial topic thanks to the British government's botched rollout of the technology; they were supposed to be fitted into 80 percent of households by 2020. But numerous delays and technical hitches, such as consumers finding their meter stopped being smart if they switched energy supplier , hindered progress. Now, a report from connectivity biz Wirepas, "The European Connectivity Trilemma," shows that it isn't just Brits who have problems, but that other European countries also have their share of smart meter issues and that no two countries have adopted the same approach. The UK's issues center on the fact that early meters used 2G or 3G cellular connections to transmit energy usage back to the supplier. These continued to be fitted until 4G versions began arriving at the end of 2024, the report says. This issue was covered by The Register back in 2023 , and again in 2024 . However, the government had already announced measures to phase out 2G and 3G networks by 2033 several years earlier, back in 2021, so it was known that any meters being fitted would have a limited lifespan. In fact, 3G services have now already been withdrawn by the networks , and they all plan to phase out 2G ahead of the 2033 deadline . BT/EE will begin closing its network from May 2029, VMO2 will start the same summer, and Vodafone aims to switch off in spring 2030. The report claims the UK now faces two substantial areas of expenditure as a result. The first covers newer, second generation (SMETS2) meters, where only the communications module needs swapping out, but even this is likely to cost £1.3 to £1.4 billion (c $1.7 to $1.9 billion) before the hardware cost of each new hub is even factored in. The other is for an estimated 7 million older, first-generation (SMETS1) meter installations, which have the cellular comms hard-wired in, so the whole meter typically needs replacing. The report authors estimate this will cost another £2.1 billion to £2.45 billion ($2.8 billion to $3.3 billion), at an indicative replacement cost of £300 to £350 per installation. This results in the estimated £4 billion in gross replacement costs, which will ultimately feed into household energy bills, adding to the very costs the government is currently trying to reduce. We asked the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), which oversees smart meters, for comment. While some of these older meters would naturally have been due for replacement as part of normal asset renewal cycles, the cell network shutdown makes the replacement program unavoidable and dictates when much of the expenditure must occur.
